stories.delivered_paragraph: Apple has reportedly delayed its first smart glasses from an early-2027 target to a June 2027 unveiling, with sales expected by year’s end, as it works on privacy safeguards and how to explain them. Bloomberg reporting cited by TechCrunch says Apple plans to stress on-device processing and no facial recognition, while avoiding the use of customer recordings for AI training. The approach is meant to distinguish the product from backlash over covert recording with rival smart glasses.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A small but growing group of Democrats is adopting its own “America First” message, arguing that money and attention should stay at home rather than support overseas wars or expensive energy exports. Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, California Rep. Ro Khanna and Nebraska independent Senate candidate Dan Osborn are among those using the phrase, Axios reports. Donald Trump’s Iran war alongside Israel has scrambled ownership of a slogan long associated with him and exposed divisions on the right.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A Democratic National Committee panel voted to make South Carolina the first voting state in the 2028 presidential primary, angering progressives who say the calendar favors the party establishment. Bernie Sanders lost South Carolina decisively in both 2016 and 2020, while Nevada, which he won in 2020, lost out for the opening slot. The dispute lands as Democrats are already fighting over 2026 primaries between left-wing challengers and centrist candidates viewed as more electable.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Israeli settlers set fire to two mosques, cars and agricultural land in West Bank villages overnight, Palestinian officials said, after a confrontation near Tal killed four Palestinians and two Israelis two days earlier. Reports also described vandalism, theft and graffiti, while Israel’s military said it sent troops to Qusra and police would collect evidence. The attacks deepen an already sharp escalation in settler violence in the occupied territory and risk further retaliatory clashes.

stories.delivered_paragraph: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged continued support for Ukraine before hosting President Volodymyr Zelensky, his first international visitor since taking office a week ago. At a naval base, Burnham is expected to announce that Britain will share intellectual property for its tablet-sized Stone Cloak electronic-warfare system so Ukraine can manufacture it at scale; the UK has already supplied thousands. The jammers are designed to help drones evade detection, extending a frontline technology partnership as Russia’s war continues.

stories.delivered_paragraph: MLB contenders are weighing last-minute roster moves before the Aug. 3 trade deadline at 6 p.m. ET, with Detroit ace Tarik Skubal and Boston closer Aroldis Chapman among the names drawing attention. Detroit’s recent surge has made a Skubal trade less certain, while several clubs—including the Dodgers, Yankees, Cubs and Phillies—are evaluating additions for a World Series push. The deadline will determine whether teams prioritize immediate October help or hold onto stars amid changing playoff races.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Charli xcx released a $4.99 digital deluxe edition of “Music, Fashion, Film” on iTunes, making three previously physical-only B-sides officially available for download. The edition adds “I Keep On Thinking Bout You Every Single Day and Night,” “Playboy Bunny” and “If You Take the Music Then What Has She Got?” to the album’s original 11 songs, plus videos. Charli had said the tracks would probably never reach streaming, making the sale a notable shift for fans who missed the limited releases.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Tadej Pogačar won the Tour de France by 6 minutes, 26 seconds for a record-tying fifth title, joining Eddy Merckx, Miguel Indurain, Bernard Hinault and Jacques Anquetil. The 27-year-old Slovenian took the yellow jersey on Stage 6 and held it through the final 15 stages, giving UAE Team Emirates-XRG a commanding victory. His nearest major rival, Jonas Vingegaard, crashed in Stage 15, but Pogačar already held a lead of more than four minutes.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Verge argues that John De Hart’s “Champagne and Bullets” deserves a place alongside cult “so bad it’s good” films such as “The Room” and “Troll 2.” De Hart wrote, directed and stars in the film, also released as “GetEven” and “Road to Revenge,” and performs an awkward country-music number called “Shimmy Slide.” The review’s case is that the movie’s strained performances and inexplicable scenes turn its lack of polish into outsider-cinema appeal.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige said Ryan Coogler chose David Jonsson as the next Black Panther after a secret meeting about six months before the planned casting search. Feige told Empire that Coogler, then focused on “Sinners,” called after meeting Jonsson and said he had found the actor for the role; Feige agreed immediately. The account confirms Coogler’s central role in shaping “Black Panther 3” and signals that Marvel has settled on its new lead well before the film’s release.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Apple will report results in what CNBC describes as the busiest week of the summer earnings season, while the Federal Reserve holds its July policy meeting. Boeing reports Tuesday, with its shares entering the week under pressure amid higher oil prices tied to renewed Middle East tensions. The combination will test whether Big Tech can sustain market expectations and whether the Fed’s message changes investors’ view of rates and risk.

stories.delivered_paragraph: U.S. stock-index futures rose and oil prices fell Sunday after the United States and Iran paused attacks, easing immediate fears of a broader disruption to energy supplies. Investors are also preparing for the Federal Reserve’s meeting and earnings from major technology companies this week. The market moves show how quickly the conflict has become a driver of both oil prices and broader risk appetite, leaving traders sensitive to any sign that the pause may not hold.
